title: The Hollow Hollow Revisited
premise: Sable Quintana has spent her life guarding the Hollow Gate in a valley where magic cannot enter, believing the seal protects the world from the old gods' hunger. When prayers begin to be answered across the realm and dragon-fire — the last force holding the gods at bay — starts to gutter, Sable is dragged beyond the valley by a fugitive priest and a disgraced dragonslayer who become her found family. She discovers the truth she has carried all along: her own blood is the key that sealed the gate, and her survival came at the cost of her mother's life. In the end, Sable must choose between reopening the gate to restore the dying dragons or keeping it shut and letting the old gods starve the world of magic forever; she finds a third path, binding herself to the gate as its living keeper, sacrificing her freedom but saving both dragons and mortals.
about_author: Cyrus Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who claims to have catalogued three thousand unpublished fantasy manuscripts before writing one. They live somewhere with unreliable weather and write only by lamplight.

chapters.title: The Valley That Forgets
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. We meet the mist-locked valley where magic cannot follow, and Sable's quiet ritual tending the Hollow Gate. A prayer slips through the seal for the first time in decades, whispering her name. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — the world outside is knocking.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Dragon ash falls on the valley, impossible since the gates closed. A wounded stranger, the priest Oren, collapses at the boundary stones, pursued by something that walks like a man but prays like a god. Emotional beat: Sable breaks her first rule to save him.

chapters.title: What the Gate Remembers
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. Recovering, Oren reveals the old gods are answering prayers again, feeding on devotion, and the last dragon-fire is guttering. He recognizes the gate sigil branded on Sable's wrist. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance born of mutual desperation.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Lie
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The village elders demand Oren be expelled; Sable covers for him, lying to the woman who raised her, Maren. Flashback fragments hint Sable's mother died at the gate. Emotional beat: guilt — the first crack in Sable's loyalty to the valley.

chapters.title: Hollow-Born
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Investigating the gate's undercrypt, Sable finds records naming her bloodline as the seal's living anchor. Her mother didn't die protecting the gate — she died becoming part of it. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: The God Who Knocks
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV. The god Vessia, wearing the body of a pilgrim queen, reaches the valley's edge and cannot cross. She begins answering the villagers' small prayers anyway, seeping through like water through stone. Emotional beat: patient, terrifying hunger.

chapters.title: Leaving the Only World
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Vessia's influence turns the valley against Sable; Maren is nearly killed by a 'blessed' mob. Sable crosses the boundary with Oren, feeling magic flood back into her veins for the first time. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of exile.

chapters.title: The Dragonslayer's Debt
chapters.summary: New character POV: Kestrel March, disgraced dragonslayer, drunk in the border city of Cinderhold, is hired to kill the 'gate-witch.' Instead she recognizes Sable's sigil as the mark of the order that ruined her. Emotional beat: bitter kinship between two women failed by duty.

chapters.title: Cinderhold Burns Brighter
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. In Cinderhold, answered prayers have bred fanaticism; temples of Vessia rise overnight. Kestrel warns Sable and Oren instead of killing them, and the three flee together. Emotional beat: found family forged in flight.

chapters.title: The Guttering Flame
chapters.summary: Oren's POV. The trio reaches the last dragon, Ysolde, ancient and half-asleep in a caldera shrine. Ysolde confirms the truth: the gate was never meant to keep gods out — it keeps them fed, slowly, and it is failing. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Prayers Answered
chapters.summary: Multiple brief POVs. Across the land, miracles bloom and rot: a healed child who no longer sleeps, a harvest that whispers. The chapter shows what a world of granted wishes costs. Emotional beat: mounting horror at salvation.

chapters.title: The Secret Between Us
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel discovers Sable's blood can reopen the gate fully — which would either free the starving dragons or unleash the gods entirely. She hides this from Sable, repeating the betrayals that broke her order. Emotional beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Vessia's Offer
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Captured briefly by Vessia's faithful, Sable is offered everything: her mother restored, the valley safe, if she opens the gate willingly. She refuses, but the temptation takes root. Emotional beat: longing dressed as virtue.

chapters.title: What Maren Never Said
chapters.summary: Maren's POV (letters). Letters reveal Maren knew Sable's origin all along and chose silence to give her an ordinary life. Sable reads them after a courier intercept. Emotional beat: fury dissolving into understanding — family is chosen twice.

chapters.title: The Order of the Broken Seal
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The trio seeks Kestrel's old order's ruins for the ritual to reforge the gate. Ambushed by Vessia's zealots; Oren is gravely wounded shielding Sable. Emotional beat: the price of survival made flesh and blood.

chapters.title: Ritual of Ash and Salt
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. In the ruins, they attempt the reforging, but it requires a willing anchor — someone to bind into the gate as her mother was. Kestrel volunteers before Sable can speak. Emotional beat: found family offering the ultimate sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Gate Opens Both Ways
chapters.summary: Climax begins, Sable's POV. The ritual tears open mid-casting as Vessia arrives in full glory. Ysolde descends, burning her final reserves. Sable sees through the opening: her mother, alive within the gate's architecture, still holding on. Emotional beat: heartbreak at the threshold.

chapters.title: Dragon-Fire and Old Hunger
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Battle at the gate: Kestrel fights her former order turned zealots, Oren dies buying seconds, Ysolde's flame wars with Vessia's hunger. Sable reaches her mother, who tells her there is a third way — not sealing, not opening, but becoming. Emotional beat: sacrifice transfigured into choice.

chapters.title: The Living Gate
chapters.summary: Climax resolution, Sable's POV. Sable binds herself to the gate as its living keeper — neither inside nor out — turning her secret into the lock itself. Vessia, unable to devour a willing keeper, is starved back to slumber. Ysolde's fire steadies. Emotional beat: transcendence through surrender.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Miracles
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The world reels: fanatics lost their voice mid-prayer, dragons wake thin but alive, and Kestrel buries Oren beside the gate. She refuses the order's offer to rebuild, choosing instead to stay near Sable. Emotional beat: mourning braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Visiting Hours
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren travels to the valley's edge, where Sable can now manifest briefly at the boundary stones. Their reconciliation is quiet and incomplete and real. Kestrel builds a cottage within sight of the gate. Emotional beat: found family holding vigil.

chapters.title: The Keeper Keeps
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Sable's POV, years later. Prayers still come, unanswered but heard; Sable tends them like a garden. Kestrel grows old nearby, telling stories to pilgrims. The last line mirrors the first: the valley forgets, but the gate remembers. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given.
